To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the concurrency alignment along the dataflow gives much faster simulation, whereas the concurrency alignment along modules/units leads to inefficient simulation.
a simple transformation of the concurrency alignment in the system models, which are written in C++-based frameworks, can lead to a significant increase of simulation performance.
the concurrency alignment in system models can be changed by a compiler front-end transformation, which can improve the simulation performance of the model by up to 50%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
providing the system designers a powerful, yet simple and natural, model for concurrency and reactivity, while providing efficient implementations of these models in the simulation kernels.
the development of a compiler front-end transformation strategy that re-assigns the concurrency in system level models, written in C++ based modeling frameworks, along the dataflow.

a compiler front-end that will automatically reassign the concurrency along a dataflow in a model written in C++-based system-level modeling environments, and thus, will provide a simple and powerful modeling of system concurrency and reactivity, while providing efficient simulation performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the transformation of the system-level design from concurrency alignment along hardware modules to concurrency alignment along dataflows is a very effective strategy to improve the simulation performance of the system-level model.

the proposed transformation strategy is an efficient and effective solution for the system designers to design their systems using their natural design methodology while achieving efficient system level simulation performance.
the transformation of the system design to a dataflow based concurrency model will lead to a better simulation performance and a more natural design model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a transformation of the concurrency in the models, which is expressed along hardware modules to concurrency along dataflow.
the concurrency re-assignment transformation can be used as a tool in a system design flow to enhance the simulation performance, while preserving the conceptual model of the system design.

the proposed transformation algorithm can be easily applied to the system models in any of the C++- based modeling frameworks such as SystemC, SpecC, and C++-SystemC, to achieve efficient simulation performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the transformation of the model from a hardware-oriented concurrency to a dataflow concurrency can lead to better performance in the simulation of system-level models, and the transformation can be performed automatically, without any change in the conceptual model of the system.

concurrency alignment along dataflows can lead to better simulation performance, and we have proposed an algorithmic transformation strategy to automatically re-align the concurrency along the hardware/software dataflows.
the transformation of concurrency alignment along units of a design to concurrency alignment along dataflows is a very effective way to improve the simulation performance of system models.
